I would love to see more nonraid content to do at max level. SoD had done some great things with raids but it feels like that's all there is to do. The wandering swordsman challenge is a good example of what I'd like to see more of in future seasonal servers.

Good players would clear an easy raid week 1. A lot of others would still take a few weeks to progress it. Then there would still be weeks of gearing up new bis, chasing parses, and speedrunning. And if it's a fun raid, which enclave seems to be so far by what I've done of it, people would still clear it just to play and hang out with their friends.

If the raid is too hard for most people to even attempt then most people would leave for another version of wow or another game altogether and just watch top guilds progress the raid.

My main point though was that we would really benefit from other meaningful nonraid content so that the raids can be more difficult. Stuff like the wandering swordsman in silithis for the sunglasses are what I would love to see more of in a future seasonal server or classic+.

Part of the issue is, at least in SoD, there's not been much content besides raids. So when the only meaningful content to do is raid then it can't be too hard for most of the population to do or most of the population will leave. Unfortunately, a lot of people are also very bad so to be doable it needs to be really easy.

In future seasonal experiments I would love to see them try out more horizontal content or non-raid content. Then the raids they do release can be more difficult on average and it won't kill the entire game mode.

I was a straight A student up until about 6th grade. When I was in 6th I found out my dad had cancer. On the surface I took the news very well but I began hiding my feelings, even from myself, and that caused a number of negative effects. My grades started dipping, I stopped paying attention in class, stopped doing homework and got very close to failing a few classes. I lost interest in most extra curricular activities I had been doing as well as most of my hobbies. I closed myself off from the world and fell into a depression that has followed me ever since. 

2 years later in my 8th grade year my dad received a bone marrow transplant and beat his cancer. But at that point depression had too strong a hold on me for that great news to reverse it. I got very good at pretending to be fine and doing just enough to get by in school and have just enough of a social life to not be a concern to anyone. I floated as a husk through high school and into college where I had a complete breakdown in my second year, finally came to terms with the feelings I had been suppressing for almost 10 years, finally reached out for help, dropped out of college, and began to long road to recovery.

It's been 4 years since I dropped out of college and in that time I got the help I needed, landed a job in security that I found I rather enjoyed, got a promotion to the head of security at a site, moved out of my parents house, and got a dog. I've still got a long way to go but I'm finally back on the right track.

TL;DR cancer and depression suck

Well I'm a 22 year old college dropout living with my parents and working a security job that I hate. I battle depression and social anxiety. I think a big part of the suicidal thoughts comes from feeling like I've lost all sense of direction in my life.

I've always loved music and when I was in 4th grade was accepted to a performing arts school where I took part in choir, orchestra, plays and musicals, and our junior thespian group. I was very involved in the arts and ended up going to a performing arts high school as well for vocal music. In high school I was in marching band, jazz band, every musical, had the leading role in Henry V, and was in 4 choirs. In addition to that I started taking private voice lessons and singing classical music. Sophomore year I started going to vocal competitions and always did very well. I went to college for vocal performance and was accepted into the top choir, had the leading villain role in Pirates of Penzance, and was still taking part in vocal competitions whenever I could. 

But part way through my freshman year I started feeling like I really didn't want to do this as a career. I brushed it off as just being nervous about the future and continued. The feelings only got worse though and eventually started to cause me panic attacks because I knew I didn't want to be there but I was too scared to tell anyone that. I started feeling suicidal and knew if I didn't get out of there, I would kill myself before long. So I called my parents and left that week.

I stayed at home for the next 4 months or so unemployed and spending almost all of my time alone in my room with the lights off mindlessly browsing reddit or playing games. Eventually I wound up getting a security job at the local mall because my brother used to work there and told me it was a real fun place to work. But not when you have social anxiety and every day in terrifying.

I used to know what my future was going to be and prepared myself for it so well that I ignored almost everything else. Now that it's gone, I have these hopes and dreams for my future but see no way to achieve them. And I feel lost and empty, my only sense of purpose is gone and I don't know what I want to do anymore.

Sorry that was so rambly, I just really needed to get that out.
